script:
Good morning. Here's your briefing for Sunday, October 4.

First up, AI & Tech.

Perplexity AI has released pplx-decider-v1-27b, an open-source decision model on Hugging Face. It's a twenty-seven billion parameter model fine-tuned from Qwen, and its model card shows it outperforming a model called Jev on several benchmarks.

German AI lab Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, an open-weight Mixture of Experts model for German and English. It has seventy-eight billion total parameters but only uses about three point five billion per token, and the weights are available on Hugging Face under an Apache two point oh license. Aleph Alpha describes the model as "sovereign," meaning it was built and trained in Europe and is designed for on-premise deployment.

A new family of four open-source decision models called Kev is now available, ranging from zero point eight billion to twenty-seven billion parameters. They are designed to be API-compatible with TypeSafe's Jev, allowing applications to switch by changing the model name and endpoint.

Cloudflare has also entered the decision model space, open-sourcing two models named Clef and Clef-flash. These are also fully Jev-API compatible, are available on Hugging Face under an Apache two point oh license, and can be run locally.

Microsoft has launched several new audio models, including MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, which debuted at number one on the Artificial Analysis benchmark. The model provides real-time transcription in sixty languages, while the new MAI-Voice-2.1 models offer voice generation in twenty-three languages.

Google researchers have detailed a framework for automated research called AIM, or Agentic Idea Management. It uses agentic components to organize research ideas, estimate their promise, and dispatch experiments, reportedly showing performance gains on several system optimization and model development tasks.

An Anthropic research post details how using Claude for scientific problems led to the creation of BootLoops, a toolkit for quantitative science calculations. The research highlights that while the AI rapidly produced technically correct code, human domain experts were still essential for ensuring the results were scientifically meaningful.

In other news, a headline from shattered dot io reads: "AWS Strands Decider 2B: Open-Source AI Agent Model [2026]".

According to a headline from cnbc dot com, Google has unveiled its latest AI model, but Wall Street is looking for a personal agent.

And a headline from trend dot az reports that Meta has launched a new AI platform to transform enterprise business.

Next, US Headlines.

Former President Trump announced a plan to send ninety-dollar checks to more than twenty million seniors to help with their Medicare costs. The promise comes ahead of the midterm elections.

Shifting to those elections, new polls show Democrats are either leading or neck-and-neck with Republicans in five key Senate races. This surge, which includes races in some Republican-leaning states, could reshape campaign strategies.

And in Tennessee, the state’s prisons chief is resigning after a recent execution attempt failed. The incident, which left the inmate unconscious and burned, has renewed national questions over whether lethal injection is a humane method of capital punishment.

Turning to Immigration & Visas.

A federal judge in California has vacated policies from the Trump administration that involved a one hundred thousand dollar fee for H one B visas.

And finally, Markets.

The major indices all finished in the green. The Nasdaq Composite led the way, climbing about one point two percent. The S&P 500 rose around zero point seven percent, and the Dow Jones added about half a percent.

It was a strong session for the big tech names on our watchlist. Alphabet was up over one and a half percent. Nvidia and Amazon both gained around one point three percent, while Apple added about one percent and Microsoft rose just under one percent.

That's your briefing. Have a great day.
